title: Lists (List<T>)
theory: An array has fixed size. A List grows and shrinks dynamically. List<string> inventory = new List<string>(); creates an empty list.
Lists use angle brackets <> to specify the item type. List<int> holds integers. List<string> holds text. The syntax reads 'List of type'.
Add items with Add(). inventory.Add("Sword"); adds a sword. Remove items with Remove() or RemoveAt().
Lists have many useful methods. Count returns the number of items. Contains() checks if an item exists. Clear() removes all items.
Use arrays for fixed-size data. Use Lists for dynamic data. Game inventories, enemy lists, and collectible items all benefit from Lists because they change during gameplay.
tryIt: Create a list of numbers, add five values, print them all, then remove one.
challenge: Create a list of player names and remove anyone whose name starts with 'Z'.
mistakes: Use angle brackets for type: List<type>.
Count is a property, not a method.
Lists use the same index access as arrays.
RemoveAt uses index; Remove uses value.
summary: Lists are dynamic arrays that grow and shrink. Use Add to insert, Remove to delete, Count to check size. Lists are essential for data that changes during runtime.
quiz: Both methods are valid for different purposes.
